title: Exploring the Frontiers of Energy Efficiency using Power Management at System Scale
problem: Exascale HPC systems face surging power demands that constrain their deployment and operation. The specific challenge is quantifying the energy savings and performance trade-offs of software-driven power management techniques like DVFS and Power Capping when applied at production scale.
motivation: Optimizing power consumption in exascale systems enables substantial cost reduction and environmental sustainability while maintaining application performance.
method: The approach combines GPU benchmarking to characterize application power profiles with three months of operational telemetry from the Frontier supercomputer. A data-driven methodology derives energy savings projections by analyzing power profiles of resource-constrained jobs and identifying candidates suitable for DVFS and power capping techniques.
key_novelty: A methodology for establishing an upper limit on best-case energy savings scenarios that is demonstrated at scale on an operational exascale supercomputer.
contributions: Data-driven telemetry-based methodology for deriving energy savings projections from application power profiles
Demonstration of up to 8.5% energy savings (1438 MWh) for resource-constrained jobs without performance degradation
Framework for HPC professionals to optimize power-performance trade-offs within constrained power budgets
Practical application and validation on the Frontier supercomputer with three months of production data
baselines: standard job scheduling without power management
primary_theme: Energy-efficient power management for exascale supercomputers
